title: Kac Kac
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Small, diamond-shaped Somali fried dough bites, lightly sweetened and fried until golden and crisp, a favorite everyday snack and a fixture at celebrations.
longDesc: Kac kac's simple, sturdy dough makes it a practical treat that keeps well for days, and its bite-sized diamond shapes have made it a common sight at Somali gatherings, served alongside tea or eaten on their own as a satisfying, not-too-sweet snack.
ingredients: 2 tbsp vegetable oil, plus more for frying
steps: Combine the flour, sugar, baking powder, cardamom, and salt in a bowl.
Whisk the egg with the oil, then combine with the dry ingredients along with enough warm water to form a firm dough.
Knead for 5-8 minutes until smooth, then rest, covered, for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough out to about half a centimeter thickness.
Cut into diamond or square shapes using a knife.
Fry the pieces in batches for 3-4 minutes, until golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and cool before serving.
chefTips: The dough should be firm, not sticky, which helps the pieces hold their shape and fry evenly.
Frying at a moderate, steady temperature ensures the pieces cook through without burning outside.
These keep well for several days in an airtight container, making them a good make-ahead treat.
commonMistakes: Making the dough too soft, which can cause the pieces to lose their shape during frying.
Frying at too high a temperature, browning the outside before the inside cooks through.
Cutting the pieces unevenly, resulting in inconsistent cooking.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 1 week.
reheating: Not applicable; served at room temperature.
healthBenefits: An occasional treat providing some protein from the egg.
culturalNote: Kac kac is a common feature at Somali celebrations and everyday gatherings alike, its sturdy, not-too-sweet character making it a reliably popular snack alongside tea.
